newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end higher, regaining their stride.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end higher, regaining their stride.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed higher in moderate trading on Wednesday, regaining their stride after stumbling the previous session, traders said.
"It's still a cheap market ... If you compare it to growth rates in the rest of the region, this bolsa still has some way to go," Westsphere broker Enrique Lerner said.

The exchange's 19-share index closed up 0.95 percent at 9,125.19 points. Volume reached 103 million shares, worth 13 billion bolivars ($27 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.

Earlier Wednesday, Salomon Brothers reiterated its overweight recommendation for Venezuelan equities as a component of its Latin American portfolio. The U.S. investment bank said high domestic liquidity and negative real interest rates left room for further gains by stocks, even though the country's current macroeconomic policy mix was probably unsustainable.
With the exchange rate appreciating in real terms, "...the stock market will provide excellent U.S. dollar returns," the report said.
Utility Electricidad de Caracas led trade with almost 10 million shares changing hands. It closed up 3.6 percent at 778.75 bolivars.
Among the issues that were traded, 22 rose, 15 fell and two closed with no change.
"After yesterday's adjustment, the market's bouncing back and investors keep on coming," said Banex broker Francisco Paolini, who sees further gains in coming days.
The bolsa's IBC index shed 2.6 percent Tuesday after eight straight record breaking sessions.
